evidence.quote: we derive vertical abundance profiles of four of Titan’s trace atmospheric species from the same 3 independent spatial regions across Titan’s disk during the same epoch (2012 to 2015)

results_numeric.quantity: HCN north enhancement vs Center near 0.1 mbar in 2015

evidence.quote: which is $\sim$16 times greater than the abundance at lower northern latitudes (Center) and a factor of 7 greater than the south

results_numeric.quantity: HC3N North/South enhancement vs Center, 2013 to 2015

evidence.quote: they increase from a factor of 50 and 34 to 75 and 61 compared to the center from 2013 to 2015

results_numeric.quantity: C3H4 North enhancement vs Center, 2014 and 2015

evidence.quote: enhancement of C$_3$H$_4$ at mid-northern latitudes with factors of 5–6 greater than the Center retrievals in 2014 and 2015

results_numeric.quantity: CH3CN North enhancement vs Center near 1 mbar

evidence.quote: increasing by a factor of 3–6.5 compared to the Center near 1 mbar

results_numeric.quantity: CH3CN relative to Cassini CIRS upper limit at 0.27 mbar

evidence.quote: We find CH$_3$CN to be a factor of $\sim5$ less than the upper limit found by (cite: nixon_10)

findings_qualitative.value: All four molecules are enhanced in the North (often South) relative to Center; retrieved temporal trends indicate continued north-to-south circulation and subsidence at the south pole.

evidence.quote: All four molecules display enhancements in the North (and often the South) compared to Center

claims.hypothesis: ALMA flux calibration data can yield spatially resolved abundance profiles of Titan's minor species
claims.experiment: NEMESIS retrievals for three latitude regions, 2012–2015
claims.result: Profiles comparable to Cassini/CIRS and previous observations, with polar enhancements muted by large beams
claims.finding: ALMA is viable for post-Cassini monitoring

evidence.quote: this work serves as a proof of concept for future measurements of Titan’s chemical abundances

claims.hypothesis: Abundances show temporal changes tracing circulation
claims.result: Increases of southern HCN, HC3N, C3H4 at altitude; Center decreases
claims.finding: Evidence for subsidence at the south pole

evidence.quote: These trends show evidence for subsidence at the southern pole

why_this_data.value: Datasets chosen by spatial resolution and date, nearest to the Paper I data

evidence.quote: Datasets were chosen based on spatial resolution and observation date

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Fractional scale height profiles rejected in favour of continuous retrievals

evidence.quote: we find that spectral fits are improved by using continuous abundance retrievals

limitations_admitted.value: Large beams average latitudes; HC3N optically thick at poles; low sensitivity above ~400 km

evidence.quote: HC$_3$N, which is optically thick at the poles where the molecule has been observed to be greatly enhanced

referee_caveats_inferred: Retrieved profiles adhere to a priori at edges of sensitivity
